problem_type: credential-bearing vendor connection fields persisted as plaintext at rest
symptom: A provider's per-connection proxy URL (Vendor.network.proxyUrl, which may embed user:pass@ userinfo) and custom request headers (Vendor.meta.extraHeaders, which may carry an Authorization / bearer value) were written to model-catalog.json in plaintext, while the API key and custom-call config were encrypted through safeStorage. Log output was already redacted, but the on-disk catalog exposed these credentials to anyone who could read the file.
direct_cause: proxyUrl and extraHeaders were stored directly on the plaintext Vendor row (network / meta) and read from there at every outbound call site. Only apiKey and customConfig had been moved into the encrypted ApiKeyRecord tier; the two network fields were never routed through an encryption boundary.
class_root: "Credential-bearing connection config" had no single encrypted boundary. Each vendor-config field decided its own at-rest representation, so apiKey/customConfig became encrypted while proxyUrl/extraHeaders stayed plaintext. Without one boundary that answers "is this field a credential payload, and if so it must ride the encrypted store", any current or future credential-bearing field can silently land as plaintext.
affected_population: Users who configured a per-connection proxy whose URL embeds proxy credentials (user:pass@host)
Users who added custom request headers carrying an Authorization or other secret value for a relay/gateway
Any future vendor connection field that can carry a secret and would otherwise inherit the plaintext-vendor-row default
entry_points: Vendor upsert / connection save (electron/catalog/catalogStore.ts applyVendorUpsert, used by manual onboarding and providerAdapter register/stage via mutateCatalog)
Catalog read (electron/catalog/catalogStore.ts readCatalog) that outbound consumers read proxy/headers from
Renderer vendor DTO + catalog export (listModelCatalogVendors / exportModelCatalogPackage via publicVendor)
Catalog forward migration v11 → v12 and the deferred write-time secret migration
Onboarding form copy that tells the user how proxy / custom headers are stored (src/i18n/locales/modelSetup.ts)
internal_only_reason: safeStorage-backed at-rest encryption of Nomi's own catalog file and the classification of which vendor-config fields are credential-bearing are internal persistence invariants. No external provider or protocol decides whether Nomi may store these fields as plaintext on the local disk.
invariants: A credential-bearing vendor connection field (proxyUrl, extraHeaders values) is encrypted through the same safeStorage tier as the API key before it is persisted; its plaintext never lands in model-catalog.json.
When safeStorage is unavailable, encrypting a credential-bearing network field fails closed and the on-disk catalog is left byte-for-byte unchanged (no plaintext fallback).
Legacy plaintext proxyUrl / extraHeaders remain readable so outbound calls keep working, and are idempotently upgraded to the encrypted representation on the next explicit vendor write.

The renderer vendor DTO and any renderer-facing catalog export never carry a credential-bearing value (proxy URL or header value); values leave the box only under an explicit include-keys export and are re-encrypted on import.
Every field on the Vendor type is classified as credential-bearing or non-credential in one registry; a new credential-bearing field that is not classified fails the type check and the guard test.
generality_proof: All at-rest encryption and decryption of credential-bearing network config flows through the single boundary electron/catalog/networkConfigStore.ts, which itself delegates to the one safeStorage primitive in electron/catalog/secrets.ts (encryptCustomSecretValue / decryptCustomSecretValue) already used by the API key and customConfig. The write path (applyVendorUpsert), the read overlay (readCatalog), and the DTO/export mask (publicVendor) all consume that boundary rather than encrypting or reading a bare field, so proxyUrl and extraHeaders share exactly one encrypted tier and one fail-closed policy. The field-classification registry (credentialConfigFields.ts) is a Record<keyof Vendor,...>, so adding any new Vendor field forces a credential classification at compile time; the guard test enforces the runtime routing.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: The single write boundary that encrypts proxyUrl and extraHeaders into the vendor credential record (via the shared safeStorage primitive) and clears the record when no network credential remains; resolveNetworkConfigForRead is its read counterpart with legacy fallback.
The one safeStorage encryption primitive shared by apiKey, customConfig, and now network config; it is the sole place that fails closed when OS secure storage is unavailable.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: applyVendorUpsert routes incoming proxyUrl/extraHeaders through applyPlainNetworkConfig and strips the plaintext off the persisted vendor row; networkConfigSecrets.test.ts asserts no plaintext reaches disk and a fresh save fails closed without safeStorage.

readCatalog overlays the decrypted (encrypted-record-wins, legacy-fallback) proxy/headers onto the internal vendor so outbound consumers read them synchronously; networkConfigSecrets.test.ts asserts the effective values resolve before and after migration.

publicVendor strips network.proxyUrl and meta.extraHeaders from every DTO; networkConfigSecrets.test.ts and customConfigSecrets.test.ts assert the DTO and no-keys export never contain a credential-bearing value.

VENDOR_CONFIG_FIELD_CLASSIFICATION is Record<keyof Vendor,...> (compile-time exhaustive) and credentialConfigFields.test.ts asserts the classification covers exactly the Vendor fields and keeps network/meta credential-bearing.

recurrence.reason: New vendor connection fields are added over time (this is the third credential-bearing field family after apiKey and customConfig); each must ride the encrypted tier rather than defaulting to the plaintext vendor row, so the encryption and the classification must live behind one boundary instead of being decided per field.
same_class_scan: Enumerated every vendor-config field on the Vendor type and classified each as credential-bearing (network, meta→extraHeaders) or non-credential in credentialConfigFields.ts.

Confirmed apiKey and customConfig already ride the encrypted ApiKeyRecord tier and that proxyUrl/extraHeaders now share that exact tier through networkConfigStore → secrets, with one fail-closed policy.

Confirmed every outbound reader (providerNetwork.providerDispatcher, catalogStore.extractVendorExtraHeaders, providerAdapter existingConnection) reads the decrypted overlay from readCatalog rather than a bare stored field.
Confirmed the renderer DTO and no-keys export drop all credential-bearing values via publicVendor, and the include-keys export re-encrypts on import.

prevention.invariant: proxyUrl and extraHeaders are encrypted and decrypted only through networkConfigStore, which delegates to the shared safeStorage primitive; no call site encrypts or reads a bare credential-bearing field.
prevention.failure_mode: safeStorage unavailable ⇒ the network-config write throws before any disk write, leaving the catalog byte-for-byte unchanged; a credential-bearing value never lands as plaintext and never reaches a DTO or export.
prevention.strategy: Keep one encrypted credential tier and one field-classification registry: every credential-bearing vendor field routes through networkConfigStore/secrets and is declared in credentialConfigFields, so a new field cannot default to the plaintext vendor row without failing the type check and guard test.

legacy_paths.rationale: This encrypts a field family that previously landed as plaintext; the legacy plaintext read path is intentionally retained inside the migration layer (resolveNetworkConfigForRead legacy fallback) so existing catalogs keep working and are upgraded idempotently on the next write. No prior implementation is replaced or removed.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: Reuses the in-tree Electron safeStorage primitive already used by apiKey and customConfig; no new dependency is introduced.

migration: Catalog version advances v11 → v12. A plain forward read never opens the keychain: a catalog carrying legacy plaintext proxyUrl/extraHeaders stays at v11 and its legacy values remain readable, exactly like the v8→v9 customConfig deferral. On the next explicit vendor write, applyVendorUpsert encrypts that vendor's legacy proxy/headers into its credential record, strips the plaintext off the vendor row, and advances the catalog to v12 once no vendor still carries legacy network plaintext. Re-running the upgrade is idempotent, and an already-encrypted value is never re-encrypted by an unrelated re-save. When safeStorage is unavailable the write fails closed and the on-disk catalog is left unchanged.
residual_risks: Legacy plaintext proxyUrl/extraHeaders remain on disk until the owning vendor is next saved; this task prevents new plaintext writes and migrates on write but does not eagerly rewrite untouched sibling vendors (matching the customConfig v8→v9 deferral).

An include-keys catalog export intentionally carries decrypted proxy/headers for portability (like the API key) so a re-import can re-encrypt them on the destination machine; a no-keys export never contains them.
